title: Italic type was invented for pocket books, not for emphasis
body: The Venetian printer Aldus Manutius introduced italic type in 1500 and in 1501 used it for an entire edition of Virgil. Cut by his punchcutter Francesco Griffo, it imitated the flowing handwriting of Italian humanists and was meant for small, portable books of popular texts. Using italics to stress a word came later and was a clear norm only by the 17th century. Early italics even paired slanted lowercase with upright capitals.
